original.target_description: Figure 3B group comparison: best unimodal versus empirical bimodal localization threshold, one-tailed matched-samples t test across six observers.

n.exclusions: No participant exclusions stated for this comparison.

es.quote: comparing best unimodal performance with bimodal performance in a one-tailed, matched samples t test produced a clearly significant difference, with t5 ⫽ 3.69 and p ⬍ 0.01.

replication.target_description: Section 3.4.1 / Figure 3B: within-participant bootstrap comparison of empirical audiovisual sensory noise against minimum auditory/visual sensory noise; 24 of 36 participants show significant variance reduction. No single group d or exact p printed for this comparison.

n.location: Sections 3.1–3.2, Participant exclusion and replacement / Trial exclusion
n.quote: All seven participants were replaced such that thirty-six participants (26 women, 10 men; 21.8 mean age, ± 2.6 years SD ) completed all three sessions. All of these datasets were included for analyses
n.sample_role: Participants; individual bootstrap comparisons of fitted sensory noise parameters in main experiment
n.exclusions: Five excluded during/after session 1 (two auditory performance, one reliability mismatch, one high visual lapse rate, one eye-tracker calibration failure); two withdrew. All seven replaced; no main-experiment participant exclusions. Trials with fixation failure/blinks excluded in 30 participants (mean 3%, maximum 12%); no trial exclusions for six with unreliable eye tracking.

es.quote: Dark diamonds indicate twenty-four participants with a significant multisensory variance reduction.

p.quote: Panel B shows that a significant multisensory variance reduction is observed for twenty-four participants, i.e., the majority of our participants

reported_success.quote: While we observed a significant variance reduction for audiovisual relative to unisensory conditions in agreement with MLE, participants weighted the visual signals significantly stronger than predicted by the MLE model.

notes: Success coding is specific to the assigned variance-reduction comparison, not the paper-wide MLE verdict. The final replication article reports individual bootstrap comparisons for this target, not a group d/p pair. The original printed t statistic is retained without conversion. Replication locator p. 10 is edition-dependent; full-text section/figure locations are supplied.
